title: Spiketrain cost & latency playbook (working)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working collateral draft describing the 'spiketrain' workload class (dense, short bursts separated by idle gaps) and pragmatic knobs to reduce tail latency and unit cost during those bursts. Focus is console-oriented guidance we can surface as a one-page help + an internal checklist for SRE/product when enabling fastpath features.

Audience:
- Console UX owners (to decide guidance copy)
- Runtime engineers (to validate assumptions + quantify knobs)
- Solutions/SEs (customer-facing recommendations)

What is spiketrain? (short)
- A sequence of microbursts (0.5–3s) arriving on a small subset of routes; high peak QPS but low average QPS. Typical for chat UI with many users typing short prompts in quick succession. Different from sustained high QPS: memory and prewarm dynamics dominate.

Key metrics we track for these drafts (definitions):
- p50/p90/p99 latency (ms) for generation-phase only (network/proxy stripped out)
- allocation-time (ms): time to assign a slot or warm a prewarmed worker
- packing inefficiency factor (PIF): ratio observed_tokens / ideal_tokens (1.0 = perfect packing)
- surge elasticity index (SEI): normalized cost increase (pct) at 10x baseline QPS
- effective $/1k tokens (post-batching and pre-caching)

Test matrix (short scenarios)
- models tested: rw-core-12B-fp16, rw-mini-7B-q4, rw-tiny-3B-fp16 (local perf profiles)
- baseline batch cap: 32 tokens/batch
- burst patterns: short-spike (0.5s at 120qps), medium-spike (2s at 60qps), train (10 spikes at 30–80qps spaced by 1s idle)

Summary table (representative numbers from lab runs, note: variability +-10%):

Scenario            | qps_peak | p50(ms) | p90(ms) | p99(ms) | alloc(ms) | PIF  | $/1k tokens
--------------------|----------|---------|---------|---------|-----------|------|-----------
rw-core-12B baseline | 60       | 85      | 150     | 420     | 120       | 1.8  | $2.30
rw-core-12B + prewarm | 60    | 72      | 110     | 190     | 20        | 1.25 | $1.95
rw-mini-7B baseline  | 120      | 42      | 90      | 260     | 90        | 2.1  | $1.10
rw-mini-7B + session-pack | 120 | 38      | 70      | 130     | 40        | 1.35 | $0.88
rw-tiny-3B baseline  | 200      | 30      | 65      | 140     | 60        | 2.5  | $0.45

Notes on table: baseline = no prewarm, opportunistic batching only. PIF decreases with session-centric packing and KV caching. Allocation time dominates p99 in our short-spike runs for larger models.

ASCII sparkline of p99 across a 12s "train" (12 time buckets, time increases left->right):
rw-core-12B baseline p99:  [ 40, 60, 120, 420, 410, 200, 140, 130, 180, 300, 250, 90 ] ms
rw-core-12B prewarm p99:   [ 30, 40, 60, 190, 170, 110, 95, 90, 110, 130, 120, 70 ] ms

Interpretation (quick):
- p99 spikes when allocation-time aligns with a microburst; prewarming collapses the worst spikes but costs more reserved GPU-time. The sweet spot for rw-core-12B in our runs was holding a small prewarm pool sized to the 95th percentile concurrent spikes.

Cost-latency tradeoff: recommended heuristics
1) If p99 > 300ms during spikes and customer SLA p99 target <= 200ms: enable session-prewarm for that route with hold-time 3–6s. Prefer low-count prewarm (2–6 GPUs) vs large scaleouts to cap PIF.
2) If average QPS is low but peak bursts are frequent (>30 spikes/hour): prefer dynamic prewarm plus short hold-time (1.5–4s) and KV cache TTL 60s.
3) For cost-sensitive customers using rw-mini-7B: enable session-pack (greedy pack by prefix) + small batch caps (16) to reduce PIF without large reserved footprint.
4) For tiny-models, rely on multiplexing and opportunistic batching; only enable prewarm when inter-arrival gaps < 400ms on average.

Operational checklist (console + SRE)
- [ ] Add "spiketrain" label for routes in Console so Optimize can surface a recommendation card.
- [ ] Expose a one-click prewarm toggle with suggested sizing (SLO-aware) in Console runtime page.
- [ ] Instrument PIF and SEI in the route dashboard (metric names: route.pif, route.sei).
- [ ] Add automated smoke test to validate prewarm hold-time changes (Jenkins job RI-1829).

Open questions / TODOs
- Need more runs across region heterogeneity (edge vs core) — are allocation times significantly different across regions? (assign to Kai)
- How does quantized rw-mini-7B compare to a tiled rw-core-12B when the conversation length variance is high? (experiment: variable-length simulator)
- Pricing model: compute actual customer-facing $/1k tokens when prewarm costs are amortized across route traffic vs reserved monthly commitment. (finance input requested)

Suggested console blurb (short):
"For chat-style UIs that see short, intense bursts of requests, we recommend enabling 'spiketrain optimizations'—session prewarm and prefix packing—to reduce tail latency by up to 60% while limiting token-unit cost increases. Try suggested sizing in the runtime panel and run the guided smoke-test."

Appendix: brief methodology notes
- Runs executed on QA cluster using synthetic traffic driver (open-source spiketrain-sim v0.3).
- Each data point is median of 10 runs; p99 computed per-run then aggregated to 50th percentile of p99 across runs to avoid outliers from infra flakiness.
- Cost measured as amortized GPU-minutes * price + per-token inference ops estimate; excludes network egress and console overhead.

Notes to self (informal)
- Keep this doc lean — final collateral should be 1 pager + 1 chart. The console card needs an image (Kai to mock).
- Crosslink with optimize/product team notes on prewarm UX (Confluence link above).
